entries.title: Psalms 107:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: No city - Or rather, no town inhabited, where they might refresh themselves.

entries.title: Psalms 107:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The Lord - Heb. Unto Jehovah, to the true God. For the Heathens had, many of them, some knowledge of the true God.

entries.title: Psalms 107:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Heart - The pride and obstinacy of their hearts. Fell - They fell into hopeless miseries.

entries.title: Psalms 107:32
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Exalt him - In public assemblies, and before all persons, as they have opportunity. Elders - The magistrates or rulers; let them not be ashamed nor afraid to speak of God's wonderful works, before the greatest of men.

entries.title: Psalms 107:33
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Rivers - Those grounds which are well watered, and therefore fruitful. And so the water - springs, here, and the standing water, ver. 35 are taken . Into - Into a dry ground, which is like a parched and barren wilderness.

entries.title: Psalms 107:34
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: For - He doth not inflict these judgments without cause, but for the punishment of sin in some, and the prevention of it in others.

entries.title: Psalms 107:35
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Water - Into a well - watered and fruitful land.

entries.title: Psalms 107:36
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Hungry - Poor people who could not provide for themselves.

entries.title: Psalms 107:39
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: They - These men, who when they are exalted by God, grow insolent and secure. Low - By God's just judgment.

entries.title: Psalms 107:40
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Contempt - Renders them despicable. Wander - Banishes them from their own courts and kingdoms, and forces them to flee into desolate wildernesses for shelter.
